lines.say: Practice day 1. I'm building 10 apps in 30 days, and today I'm building how I'll film it.
Hey folks, here's what I did in the past hour.
First, I turned a messy brainstorm into one page. 10 apps, 30 days, a long video and a short every day.
Every decision is answered here. Three practice days, and Day 1 is this Friday.
My first plan was to talk over clips later. I tried it, and it didn't feel natural.
So now I do a quick recap like this one every hour.

recaps.summary: I started the day with a rambling voice brainstorm about filming this 10-apps-in-30-days challenge and turned it into one review page, where I answered every decision by clicking: three practice days first, series Day 1 on Friday 25 September, one 20-minute video a day for my free Skool community and one 40-second short on five channels. My first plan was to record my screen silently while working and talk over the clips in the evening. I actually tried it, and it felt unnatural, because I'm used to clicking through my work while I explain it. So I switched to a 1–2 minute recap every hour, clicked through live in Screen Studio, which needs no trimming. The open question was how Claude would know what ten different agents did in an hour, and the answer is that every Claude Code session keeps a timestamped log, so a small script reads the last hour of all of them. By the end of the hour the whole pipeline was decided and written down.

recaps.title: Splitting the Content Skills

lines.say: Hey folks, here's what I did in the past 45 minutes.
I asked if I should move task tracking into Notion, but decided html-worker was already working fine, so I stuck with it.
I previewed a day-1 tasks page with tabs per hour and a plus button for a new hour summary, then reworked the list into what I'm showing, how to show it, and the details.
Partway through I realized the task checklist and the hourly recap are two different jobs, so I split what was going to be one skill into two.
Built daily-content-system with hour.py, page.html and server.py, this one runs the real one-off Claude call for each hour's recap.
Built daily-tasks separately with its own server and page, just for tracking today's checklist.
Moved today's real data into the new formats and deleted the old mock files, so both pages open on real content now.
Lesson: things that look like one feature, like a task list and a content recap, can actually be two separate jobs, worth splitting before you build instead of after.
Next: finish the end-to-end test of the hourly recap and the plus button, then start on the Remotion edit.

I first asked whether to use Notion for day 1 tasks and goals, but decided to stick with the html-worker approach I already had running. I started an end-to-end test of the plus-button recap and the task generator, but that test wasn't finished by the end of the session.

recaps.title: Practice Day 1 Recap
recaps.summary: Today was the first of three practice days before the real 10-apps-in-30-days series starts this Friday. I started by turning a rambling brainstorm into one decision page, locking the format: one 20-minute video a day plus a 40-second short on five channels. My first plan was to record my screen silently and narrate it later, but that felt unnatural, so I switched to filming a short recap live every hour instead. I built the first version of that pipeline, including a script that reads the last hour of every agent's logs so Claude knows what happened. In the second half of the day I sat down to test that pipeline, but instead realized the daily task checklist and the hourly content recap were actually two separate jobs. So I split one planned skill into two, daily-content-system and daily-tasks, each with its own server and page, moved today's real data into them, and threw out the early mockups. By the end of the day the pipeline was locked and the tools were rebuilt around real content, but the end-to-end test and the Remotion edit are still ahead.

lines.say: My first plan for filming this whole challenge didn't survive one real try, so I ditched it after an hour.
This is Practice Day 1 of building 10 apps in 30 days, three practice days before the real series starts this Friday.
